text: At that time, declares the LORD, I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they shall be my people.
This is what the LORD says: The people who survived the sword found grace in the wilderness; Israel went out to find its rest.
From far away the LORD appeared to me: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have drawn you to myself with faithful love.
Again I will build you, and you shall be rebuilt, O virgin Israel. Again you will take up your tambourines and go out dancing with the joyful.
Again you will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria; the planters will plant and enjoy the fruit.
For there will come a day when the watchmen call out on the hills of Ephraim, "Rise up, let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God!"
For this is what the LORD says: Sing with joy for Jacob; shout aloud at the head of the nations. Proclaim it, give praise, and say, "LORD, save your people, the remnant of Israel!"

versions.text: For this is what the LORD says: Sing with joy for Jacob; shout for the chief of the nations. Proclaim it, give praise, and say, "LORD, save your people, the remnant of Israel!"
versions.explanation: בְּרֹאשׁ הַגּוֹיִם most naturally means "at the head/forefront of the nations," i.e., where the proclamation is made, rather than naming Jacob "the chief of the nations." The revised wording keeps the parallel imperative and reads more clearly aloud.

text: See, I am bringing them from the land of the north, gathering them from the ends of the earth—among them the blind and the lame, the pregnant woman and the one in labor together; a great assembly will return here.

They will come with weeping, and with pleas for mercy I will lead them back. I will guide them to streams of water on a level path where they will not stumble, for I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
Hear the word of the LORD, you nations, and declare it in the distant coastlands: He who scattered Israel will gather him and will guard him as a shepherd guards his flock.
For the LORD has ransomed Jacob and redeemed him from the hand of one stronger than he.

They will come and sing for joy on the heights of Zion; they will stream to the goodness of the LORD—the grain, the new wine, and the oil, the young of the flocks and herds. Their life will be like a well-watered garden, and they will never languish again.
Then the young woman will rejoice in the dance, and the young men and the old together. I will turn their mourning into gladness; I will comfort them and give them joy instead of sorrow.
I will fill the priests with abundance, and my people will be satisfied with my goodness, declares the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: A voice is heard in Ramah, mourning and bitter weeping—Rachel weeping for her children, refusing to be comforted for her children, because they are no more.
This is what the LORD says: Keep your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for there is a reward for your labor, declares the LORD; they will return from the land of the enemy.
There is hope for your future, declares the LORD; your children will return to their own land.
I have surely heard Ephraim grieving: "You disciplined me, and I was disciplined, like an untrained calf. Bring me back, and I will return, for you are the LORD my God.
After I turned away, I repented; after I came to understand, I struck my thigh in grief. I was ashamed and humiliated, for I bore the disgrace of my youth."

Is not Ephraim my dear son, the child in whom I delight? For as often as I speak against him, I still remember him. Therefore my heart yearns for him; I will surely have mercy on him, declares the LORD.
Set up road markers for yourself; put up guideposts. Fix your mind on the highway, the road you traveled. Return, O virgin Israel, return to these cities of yours.
How long will you waver, unfaithful daughter? For the LORD has created something new on the earth: a woman shall encompass a man.

This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Once again they will speak these words in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I restore their fortunes: "May the LORD bless you, O dwelling of righteousness, O holy mountain."
The people of Judah and all its towns will live there together—farmers and those who move about with their flocks.

versions.text: Judah and all its cities will live there together—farmers and those who move about with their flocks.
versions.explanation: As it stands, the subject reads as though the cities themselves "live there." Supplying "the people of" clarifies that the inhabitants are meant, which is the sense of the Hebrew collective.

text: For I have satisfied the weary soul, and every languishing soul I have filled.

versions.text: For I will refresh the weary soul, and every languishing soul I will fill.
versions.explanation: Both Hebrew verbs are perfects (הִרְוֵיתִי, מִלֵּאתִי). Rendering them as completed action (prophetic perfect) preserves the force of the original; the future tense flattens the emphatic declaration.

text: At this I awoke and looked around, and my sleep had been sweet to me.
The days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of people and the seed of animals.
And just as I watched over them to uproot and tear down, to overthrow, destroy, and bring disaster, so I will watch over them to build and to plant, declares the LORD.
In those days they will no longer say, "The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge."
Instead, each will die for his own guilt; whoever eats the sour grapes, his own teeth will be set on edge.
The days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt—my covenant that they broke, though I was their husband, declares the LORD.

But this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the LORD: I will put my law within them and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.

No longer will anyone teach his neighbor or his brother, saying, "Know the LORD," for they will all know me, from the least of them to the greatest, declares the LORD. For I will forgive their guilt and remember their sin no more.

This is what the LORD says—he who gives the sun for light by day, who fixes the order of the moon and the stars for light by night, who stirs up the sea so its waves roar; the LORD of hosts is his name:

versions.text: This is what the LORD says—he who gives the sun for light by day, who set in order the moon and the stars for light by night, who stirs up the sea so its waves roar; the LORD of hosts is his name:
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has a single participial construction ("who gives... the fixed orders of moon and stars"); the shift to past tense "who set in order" breaks the parallel present-tense rhythm of the surrounding participles ("gives," "stirs up") and obscures the link to the חֻקִּים ("fixed orders") echoed in v.36.

text: Only if these fixed orders depart from before me, declares the LORD, will the offspring of Israel ever cease to be a nation before me, for all time.

versions.text: Only if this fixed order departs from before me, declares the LORD, will the offspring of Israel ever cease to be a nation before me.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew הַחֻקִּים הָאֵלֶּה is plural ("these fixed orders"), matching the plural decrees of sun, moon, stars and sea in v.35, and the closing phrase כָּל־הַיָּמִים ("all the days / for all time") is not represented in the current rendering.

text: This is what the LORD says: Only if the heavens above can be measured and the foundations of the earth below explored will I reject all the offspring of Israel for all they have done, declares the LORD.
The days are coming, declares the LORD, when this city will be rebuilt for the LORD, from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
The measuring line will stretch out farther, straight to the hill of Gareb, and then turn toward Goah.

The whole valley of the dead bodies and the ashes, and all the terraced fields as far as the Kidron Valley, to the corner of the Horse Gate on the east, will be holy to the LORD. The city will never again be uprooted or torn down.
